Hi Samir — really glad the demo landed. I put together high-level answers below and will loop in our pricing and engineering leads for the precise math and sample invoice.

Summary (short):
- Token accounting: we bill per token consumed (prompt tokens + generated tokens) measured by our canonical tokenizer. Streaming vs. non-streaming: billing is identical — you pay for tokens produced, but streaming just changes latency/response delivery.
- Context length: you’re billed only for tokens actually present in the request/response. Large model context (e.g., 48k) only increases cost if you include that context in the request. We enforce a max request token limit per model variant; if a conversation archives history server-side and you later rehydrate a subset, you’ll be charged for the tokens sent in that call.
- Rounding/minimums: by default hosted metered accounts have a small-call quantum of 5 tokens per API call (we round up to nearest 5 tokens for each request) to avoid microbilling overhead. Committed customers can opt out (no per-call quantum) in exchange for a committed monthly spend.

Conservative example (pilot):
- Prompt: 180 tokens, Model output: 420 tokens => 600 tokens billed (rounded to nearest 5 => stays 600).
- Many tiny calls: 40 calls of 3 tokens each => raw 120 tokens billed, but with the 5-token quantum each call rounds to 5 => 40 * 5 = 200 tokens (we can waive this for committed pilots).

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik (engineering) to confirm rounding logic and provide a one-page technical note with a few sample calculations.
2) Marissa (commercial) to propose a pilot pricing matrix (metered vs. small committed bucket + one-time onboarding credit).
3) We’ll send a short sample invoice and a DocuSign link once you confirm the preferred pilot structure.

Attaching a short note — will follow up once Karthik and Marissa chime in.

Hi all — technical clarification below and attached a one-page PDF with worked examples.

Technical note (summary):
- Tokenization: we use our canonical tokenizer (compatible with most open models). Billed tokens = tokens present in the HTTP request body (prompt, system messages, instructions) + tokens generated by the model.
- Streaming: billed the same as non-streaming. If you cancel mid-stream, you’re billed for tokens already produced.
- Context windows: only tokens actually included in a call are billed. If you send a trimmed history, cost reflects trimmed tokens.
- Rounding: hosted metered accounts are charged per-call rounded up to the nearest 5-token quantum. The rounding happens at request-finalization time (after generation) — we do NOT double-round on both prompt and response separately; rounding applies to the total token count for that request.
- Aggregation exception: for pilots we can offer an aggregation waiver: instead of per-call rounding, we compute total tokens across the pilot timeframe and apply rounding only on the final aggregated total (this prevents microservice chatter from inflating cost). This is a one-time concession and must be flagged in the SOW.

Worked examples (attached):
- Example A: 180 + 420 = 600 -> billed 600 (quantum 5 => no change)
- Example B: 40 calls x 3 tokens raw = 120 -> per-call quantum = 40 x 5 = 200 billed; with aggregation waiver = 120 billed.

Attachment: rounding_examples.pdf (pdf) — contains tabular examples and a small script snippet to replicate our token counts.

-Karthik
